I made a logo for a fictional generative AI company called **loam** (named after soil, where things grow). It uses organic shapes and a palette of seven earthy neutrals. I checked every PNG by eye after rendering.

**The concept:** The symbol is five stacked pebble-like shapes, like a river stone cut open or tree growth rings. Each layer is darker than the one outside it and sits a little further toward the upper right. They narrow toward a dark seed in the middle, the idea being something emerging layer by layer, the way a generative model builds an output. The lettering is custom-drawn with soft rounded strokes. The "l" has a little curled foot, and the bowls of the "o" and "a" are slightly irregular to echo the pebble shape.

**Files in `./output/`:**
- `loam-logo-light.svg` / `.png`: the main version, symbol plus name, dark text on an off-white background
- `loam-logo-dark.svg`: the same on a near-black background, with the layer colours reversed so the seed is light
- `loam-mark.svg`: the symbol on its own, with a transparent background
- `loam-app-icon.svg` / `.png`: the symbol on a rounded square (1024 px PNG)
- `loam-brand-sheet.png`: a 1600×1000 overview showing both versions, the app icon, the palette with hex codes, and the symbol at 96 px down to 16 px

All files are well under 2 MB. The logo SVGs are made entirely of shapes with no fonts, so they look the same everywhere. Only the brand sheet's labels use a system font (Helvetica), and they're baked into the PNG.

**Things to know:**
- At small sizes and in the app icon, the off-centre dark core can look a bit like an eye. I softened this by removing a light highlight in the centre, but some of that reading remains.
- At 16–24 px, the faint outer layer almost disappears against the light background.
- The app icon PNG has white corners outside the rounded square, not transparent ones.

**Source:** `src/build.mjs` generates all the SVGs. `src/render.sh` rebuilds everything and exports the PNGs using macOS Quick Look and ffmpeg.
